story.title: The Story of Help Us Green
paragraphs_en: Bholu the bear had a busy day. He was a reporter in the television channel Aaj Ka Jungle. Today, he had to take the interview of Ankit Aggarwal, the founder of Help Us Green. He had set up the company in 2015. The company specialised in recycling flowers into vermicompost. They made many creative items out of it. Bholu: Hello, everyone, today we have one of India’s most creative businessmen amongst us. Not only does he run a huge organization but saves the environment while running it.

Welcome, Mr. Ankit Aggarwal, how are you? Could you tell us a little something about your company, Help Us Green? Ankit Aggarwal: Hi Bholu. I am well. Our company – Help Us Green recycles flower waste. By recycling this waste, we achieve many purposes, we save our rivers, promote organic materials and produce biodegradable products in a creative way. Bholu: You said something about saving our rivers, how does this happen? Ankit Aggarwal: Hi Bholu. I am well. Our company – Help Us Green recycles flower waste. By recycling this waste, we achieve many purposes, we save our rivers, promote organic materials and produce biodegradable products in a creative way.

Bholu: You said something about saving our rivers, how does this happen? Ankit Aggarwal: You would have definitely noticed that devotees from various religious places throw a lot of flowers after worship in our rivers and ponds. This is especially true of Ganga and Yamuna. Many tonnes of roses, jasmines, daffodils, lilies and lotuses are thrown into water bodies. They float on water bodies and rot away. They pollute the water a lot. I observed that foam had formed on these flowers. On examining it closely, my team and I realized that this foam was actually a fully biodegradable type of fibre. We thought that we should use this fibre creatively. Even the water we use for recycling is completely purified. Bholu: So you started making vermicompost out of this foam of flowers that you call florafoam. You used it to create incense sticks (called phool).

Ankit Aggarwal: Not just incense sticks, it is also used in biodegradable packing of electronics. It has replaced thermocol in many instances as it is 27% cheaper than thermocol. This is especially good as thermocol is one of the world’s biggest polluters. The biodegradable packaging can be disposed off by burying it into the earth. We aim to make 11 tonnes of such material everyday and are opening a plant in Kanpur for that purpose. Bholu: I understand. Are you thinking of launching any new products? Ankit: Yes, definitely, our next range of products also include mosquito repellents and diabetes medicines. I really look forward to this expansion. I am also planning to expand our units to Mathura and Vrindavan since the water bodies out there tend to get very polluted. We have also started manufacturing leather from flower waste. It can be dyed by beautiful natural colours and looks very stylish! We plan to sell this leather to top designers.

Bholu: This sounds great. What do you consider as your biggest victory in this entire process? Ankit: I feel that my biggest victory has been to save our Ganges from pollution, in whatever little way we could, and the empowerment of rural women. Mostly village women are involved in our factory-work. My aim is to generate full-time employment for five thousand women and empower them economically. Bholu: That is truly an inspiring idea. What is the one factor that really helped you?

Ankit: I think the fact that the products are made from flowers that were once offered to gods, have made our products seem sacred. Some people thought that we will not be able to sell our products as they have been made from waste, but this was entirely wrong. People were very happy to buy them. This Diwali we even ran out of stock! Bholu: That is indeed great. You have already won many prestigious awards for your initiative. I wish you more awards, more luck for your future endeavours and wish that many others get inspired by you and work towards saving our rivers. Thanks a lot for humouring us. Ankit: Thanks, this was my pleasure.
